CURRICULUM VITAE

TOMISLAV MESARIĆ
Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Butcher-trained meat counter professional with four years of customer service experience at Dolac Market Hall. Experienced in weighing and pricing orders, operating a till, rotating cold-room stock using FIFO, and maintaining clean equipment. Additional hands-on experience preparing whole lambs and suckling pigs, developing fresh sausage products, and recording temperature and weight-loss data during a dry-ageing trial. Basic HACCP knowledge.

KEY SKILLS
• Meat counter customer service and order handling
• Weighing, pricing and till operation
• Cold-room stock rotation (FIFO)
• Preparation of whole lambs and suckling pigs
• Fresh sausage preparation and product development
• Cleaning slicers, mincers and counter areas
• Basic HACCP knowledge and hygiene routines
• Customer-facing English

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Meat Counter Assistant / Butcher | Mesnica Kod Ante, Dolac Market Hall
Current role | Four years of meat-counter customer service
• Serve customers, weigh and price their orders, and operate the till.
• Rotate cold-room stock every morning, placing older stock at the front.
• Clean slicers and the mincer each evening.
• Prepare, butcher, season and deliver whole lambs and suckling pigs for spit-roasting orders.

SELECTED PROJECTS
Shop Sausage Range | Mesnica Kod Ante | 2020–Present
• Developed the shop’s lamb merguez recipe and adjusted the ćevapi mix to 70% beef and 30% lamb following customer feedback.
• The ćevapi received second place at the Zagreb County craft meat fair (Sajam mesnih proizvoda) in 2023.
• Make approximately 40 kg of fresh sausage per week during the busy season.

Wedding and Party Catering | Mesnica Kod Ante | 2022–2025
• Prepared, butchered, seasoned and delivered whole lambs and suckling pigs for spit-roasting at three weddings and approximately ten family parties per year.
• Prepared an order of four lambs and two pigs for a 180-guest wedding in Samobor in 2024.

Dry-Aged Beef Trial | Mesnica Kod Ante | 2024
• Ran a six-week trial of dry-ageing beef ribs for 21 and 28 days in a rented cabinet; recorded weight loss and temperature.
• The shop now sells dry-aged rib by pre-order, at approximately 15 kg per month.

Stall Closing Routine | Tržnica Dolac Meat Hall | 2017
• Wrote a one-page closing and cleaning checklist for the slicer, mincer, counter and floor drain following a hygiene inspection remark. The checklist remains in use at the stall.

EDUCATION & TRAINING
Butcher Training | Food Trades School | 2015
HACCP | Basic knowledge
Master Butcher Exam (Majstorski Ispit) | Preparing; exam planned for spring 2027

LANGUAGES
English | Good for customer service


COVER LETTER

Dear FreshCart Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant position at your Zagreb-Jarun store. I completed butcher training at the Food Trades School and have four years of experience serving customers at the meat counter at Dolac Market Hall. I would bring practical counter experience, care with hygiene and a strong focus on helpful, honest product advice.

In my current role, I weigh and price orders, operate the till, rotate cold-room stock every morning using FIFO, and clean the slicer and mincer each evening. I also prepare whole lambs and suckling pigs for spit-roasting orders. Alongside this work, I developed the shop’s lamb merguez recipe and adjusted its ćevapi mix in response to customer feedback; the ćevapi received second place at the Zagreb County craft meat fair in 2023.

I have basic HACCP knowledge and have recorded temperature and weight-loss data during a dry-ageing trial. I understand the importance of reliable routines, clean equipment and well-managed stock in providing fresh food and maintaining customers’ trust. FreshCart’s emphasis on knowledgeable, approachable staff and honest advice at the counter is especially appealing to me.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my meat-counter experience and practical butchery skills could contribute to the FreshCart team.

Kind regards,
Tomislav Mesarić

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional and well structured. It clearly identifies the role, summarizes relevant butcher training and four years of meat-counter experience, and uses concrete evidence such as FIFO stock rotation, equipment cleaning and the award-winning sausage product. The dry-ageing and HACCP references add credibility without making the letter unnecessarily long. One phrase overstates evidence in the candidate information: the letter claims a strong focus on product advice, but the source material confirms customer service rather than specific advice on cuts, quantities or preparation.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: ATS compatibility is strong for a cover letter. The document uses standard text formatting, conventional paragraphs, readable job-related terminology and relevant keywords including “butcher training,” “meat counter,” “HACCP,” “FIFO,” “temperature,” “weight-loss,” “slicer,” “mincer” and “till.” It should have a high AI-screening probability for the two stated must-have requirements. The forklift licence is correctly not claimed. The letter does not include unsupported supermarket, self-service packaging or forklift experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns strongly with FreshCart’s priorities of fresh food, hygiene, reliable routines, approachable customer service and practical experience. It directly demonstrates the required butcher training, more than two years of meat-counter experience, and basic HACCP knowledge. It also provides relevant evidence for stock rotation, clean equipment and customer-facing work. The candidate’s material indicates no forklift licence, which is only a nice-to-have. It also indicates no supermarket, tray-sealer or self-service labelling-scale experience; these are role-context gaps rather than defects in the letter and are not stated as must-have requirements. The letter does not claim experience advising customers specifically on cuts, quantities or preparation, which is appropriate because that capability is not clearly documented in the source material.
critique.improvement_instructions: CRITICAL — In the opening paragraph, replace “I would bring practical counter experience, care with hygiene and a strong focus on helpful, honest product advice” with a fully supported statement such as “I would bring practical counter experience, reliable hygiene routines and a strong focus on helpful customer service.” This removes the unsupported claim about product advice while preserving alignment with FreshCart’s customer-service priorities.
critique.critical_issues:
Potential unsupported claim: “a strong focus on helpful, honest product advice” is not established in the Original Candidate Information. The source material confirms four years of customer service, but does not specifically confirm advising customers on cuts, quantities or preparation. Remove or revise this phrase as specified in the improvement instructions.
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- “a strong focus on helpful, honest product advice”

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, and well tailored to the Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant role. It clearly presents the candidate's butcher training, four years of meat-counter experience, customer service, FIFO stock rotation, till operation, equipment cleaning, HACCP knowledge, and practical product-development experience. The quantified and distinctive evidence—such as the award-winning ćevapi recipe and dry-ageing records—gives the application credibility and impact. The closing is appropriate, although the final paragraph is somewhat conventional and could be slightly more specific about the value the candidate would bring to the counter team.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter uses a simple, ATS-friendly structure with a clear heading, standard paragraphs, and no problematic tables, graphics, columns, or unusual formatting. It contains important matching terms including “butcher training,” “meat counter,” “HACCP,” “FIFO,” “till,” “cold-room stock,” “slicer,” “mincer,” “weigh,” “price,” and “customer service.” It does not claim unsupported forklift, supermarket, self-service packaging, or tray-sealer experience. For slightly stronger keyword alignment, the letter could use the job ad's exact phrase “Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant” in the opening and explicitly connect temperature records to food-safety routines, without claiming that the candidate performed hygiene checks that are not documented.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is very strong for the stated must-have requirements. The candidate has completed butcher training, four years of meat-counter experience, basic HACCP knowledge, FIFO stock rotation, customer-facing experience, and relevant temperature-recording experience. The letter also reflects FreshCart's culture signals of reliability, hygiene, approachable customer service, fresh food, and honest product advice. The candidate's experience is from a market meat stall rather than a supermarket, and the original information states that they have not used tray sealers or self-service labelling scales; these are role-experience differences rather than defects in the letter. The candidate also lacks the advertised forklift licence, which is only a nice-to-have. The letter appropriately does not imply possession of that licence or advanced HACCP certification.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENT:
1. In the opening paragraph, change “I am applying for the Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant position at your Zagreb-Jarun store” to “I am applying for the Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant position at FreshCart’s Zagreb-Jarun store.” This keeps the exact job title while making the employer and store reference read more naturally.

2. In the third paragraph, change “I have basic HACCP knowledge and have recorded temperature and weight-loss data during a dry-ageing trial” to “I have basic HACCP knowledge and have maintained temperature records during a dry-ageing trial, alongside recording weight loss.” This places the food-safety-relevant evidence first and makes the wording more direct without overstating the candidate’s HACCP level.

3. In the final paragraph, replace “I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my meat-counter experience and practical butchery skills could contribute to the FreshCart team” with “I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my meat-counter experience, reliable hygiene routines and practical butchery skills could support FreshCart’s fresh-food counter.” This gives the closing a more specific connection to the advertised role and company priorities.
